about: The Wizard's first call comes for certain on his first clock after the visitor leaves the barrow, here on the second 'wait' (three moves and ninety seconds each); he casts Fantasize, and the room's illusion holds for the length of the spell, listed on 'look' and refused in the narrator's voice, and is gone when it ends, which in the first thirty moves is three minutes. The sword does not glow for a call that begins and ends in one move. Round 4: the illusion's refusal opens with the verb's own clause, an eye for looking and a blow for striking.

expect.words: A strange little man in a long cloak appears suddenly in the room. He is wearing a high pointed hat embroidered with astrological signs. He has a long, stringy, and unkempt beard.

The Wizard draws forth his wand and waves it in your direction. It begins to glow with a faint blue glow. He peers at you from under his bushy eyebrows, as though you were not at all what he had been expecting, and had turned up anyway.

His eye goes to your hands, which hold nothing he values, and he relaxes a little: whatever you have come for, you have not found it yet. It is all south of the ravine, his look says, every treasure the Empire mislaid, and much good may it do you; the pearls nearest, behind a stone door that asks a question, and the rest further in, past a room that will not keep still.
The Wizard, in a deep and resonant voice, speaks the word "Fantasize!" He then vanishes, cackling gleefully.
